sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是99%隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: We live in a post-billiards world.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个后台球时代的世界。

sentences.en: There was an age of billiards, and it has been over for so long,
sentences.zh: 曾经有一个台球的时代，而它已经结束了那么久，

sentences.en: most of us have no idea how huge billiards once was.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人甚至不知道台球曾经有多么庞大。

sentences.en: A hundred years ago, there were 830 pool halls in my city of Chicago.
sentences.zh: 一百年前，在我的城市芝加哥，有830家台球厅。

sentences.en: Now, if you add up all the gas stations, all the McDonald's,
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你把所有的加油站、所有的麦当劳，

sentences.en: and all the Starbucks in Chicago right now,
sentences.zh: 以及现在芝加哥所有的星巴克加起来，

sentences.en: you'd be nowhere close to that number.
sentences.zh: 你甚至都无法接近那个数字。

sentences.en: You'd be a little under 600, if you want to be exact.
sentences.zh: 如果你想精确一点，大概不到600家。

sentences.en: And I know you do, you beautiful nerds.
sentences.zh: 我知道你们很想知道，你们这些可爱的书呆子。

sentences.en: Today, Chicago has fewer than 10 pool halls.
sentences.zh: 如今，芝加哥的台球厅不到10家。

sentences.en: That is Dan Weissman, reporter, Chicagoan.
sentences.zh: 那是丹·维斯曼，记者，芝加哥人。

sentences.en: Dan originally reported this story for a marketplace.
sentences.zh: 丹最初是为一个市场节目报道这个故事的。

sentences.en: So, billiards.
sentences.zh: 所以，台球。

sentences.en: Not what it used to be.
sentences.zh: 不再是当年的那个台球了。

sentences.en: But this is a post-billiards world in a much more profound sense,
sentences.zh: 但这是一个更深刻意义上的后台球时代，

sentences.en: because the growth of billiards led to the development of a material that,
sentences.zh: 因为台球的发展催生了一种材料，

sentences.en: for better or worse, came to define the modern world.
sentences.zh: 无论好坏，它最终定义了现代世界。

sentences.en: I just want to say one word to you.
sentences.zh: 我只想对你们说一个词。

sentences.en: Just one word.
sentences.zh: 就一个词。

sentences.en: You listening?
sentences.zh: 在听吗？

sentences.en: Plastics.
sentences.zh: 塑料。

sentences.en: This story starts with a guy named Michael Phelan.
sentences.zh: 这个故事从一个叫迈克尔·费兰的人开始。

sentences.en: Who's regarded by everybody as really the father of American billiards.
sentences.zh: 他被所有人公认为美国台球之父。

sentences.en: That's Michael Seamus.
sentences.zh: 那是迈克尔·谢默斯。

sentences.en: He's the author of the illustrated Encyclopedia of Billiards.
sentences.zh: 他是《插图台球百科全书》的作者。

sentences.en: Phelan was a brilliant player, but he also raised awareness of the sport,
sentences.zh: 费兰不仅是一位出色的球手，他还提高了这项运动的知名度，

sentences.en: promoted it, arranging the biggest big money matches.
sentences.zh: 推广它，并安排了最大的高额奖金比赛。

sentences.en: Phelan was totally remarkable, because he was everything.
sentences.zh: 费兰非常了不起，因为他无所不能。

sentences.en: He was an all-around-everything guy.
sentences.zh: 他是个全能型的人才。

sentences.en: He started a huge billiards hall in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 他在旧金山开了一家巨大的台球厅。

sentences.en: He patented a new kind of billiard cushion.
sentences.zh: 他为一种新型台球库边申请了专利。

sentences.en: And then, he took the money he had won playing billiards and writing books on billiards,
sentences.zh: 然后，他用打台球和写台球书赚来的钱，

sentences.en: and used it to become the first big manufacturer of billiard tables and equipment.
sentences.zh: 用它成为了台球桌和器材的第一大制造商。

sentences.en: Phelan created the age of billiards in the U.S.,
sentences.zh: 费兰在美国开创了台球时代，

sentences.en: and he felt that to further popularize the game of billiards...
sentences.zh: 他觉得为了进一步普及台球运动……

sentences.en: And sell more tickets to matches, and sell more books, and sell more equipment,
sentences.zh: 为了卖出更多的比赛门票，卖出更多的书，卖出更多的器材，

sentences.en: he would need to standardize the gear.
sentences.zh: 他需要将装备标准化。

sentences.en: Because if tables and balls weren't the same from one location to another,
sentences.zh: 因为如果台球桌和球在不同地方不一样，

sentences.en: well, you were basically playing a different game every time you went somewhere new.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那你每次去一个新的地方，基本上都是在玩一种不同的游戏。

sentences.en: But standardizing the billiard ball was no easy task.
sentences.zh: 但要将台球标准化并非易事。

sentences.en: It's a very, very high standard to meet.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常非常高的标准。

sentences.en: The billiard ball has to have certain physical properties.
sentences.zh: 台球必须具备某些物理特性。

sentences.en: It has to rebound properly.
sentences.zh: 它必须能够正常反弹。

sentences.en: It has to be of uniform density.
sentences.zh: 它必须具有均匀的密度。

sentences.en: And at the time, there was really only one material that would do.
sentences.zh: 在当时，真的只有一种材料可以胜任。

sentences.en: Ivory.
sentences.zh: 象牙。

sentences.en: Which was not cheap.
sentences.zh: 这可不便宜。

sentences.en: Going to Africa, shooting elephants, that is dangerous and expensive.
sentences.zh: 去非洲，射杀大象，这既危险又昂贵。

sentences.en: Not to mention horrible.
sentences.zh: 更不用说太可怕了。

sentences.en: And people for decades had been trying to find substitutes for ivory.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，人们一直在尝试寻找象牙的替代品。

sentences.en: And they tried a variety of materials, including even metal balls, iron balls,
sentences.zh: 他们尝试了各种材料，甚至包括金属球、铁球，

sentences.en: which really don't perform well.
sentences.zh: 这些球的表现确实不佳。

sentences.en: Iron billiard balls just weren't the same.
sentences.zh: 铁台球就是不一样。

sentences.en: Ivory balls had just the right weight, the most even roll, the best rebound off the cue
sentences.zh: 象牙球拥有恰到好处的重量，最均匀的滚动，最棒的反弹感，无论是从球杆上，

sentences.en: stick, off each other, off the side of the table.
sentences.zh: 从彼此身上，还是从球台边缘。

sentences.en: Nothing was as good.
sentences.zh: 没有什么比它更好了。

sentences.en: And not only that, only the best grade ivory would do.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，只有最高等级的象牙才行。

sentences.en: In fact, when you look at records from the ivory trade, the top grade of ivory is actually
sentences.zh: 事实上，当你查看象牙贸易的记录时，最高等级的象牙实际上

sentences.en: called billiard ball ivory.
sentences.zh: 被称为台球级象牙。

sentences.en: And billiard balls required a lot of billiard ball-grade ivory.
sentences.zh: 而且台球需要大量的台球级象牙。

sentences.en: Unlike the ivory on piano keys, which were just a veneer over wood, billiard balls had
sentences.zh: 与钢琴键上的象牙不同，那只是木头上的薄薄一层，台球

sentences.en: to be made of 100% solid ivory.
sentences.zh: 必须由100%的实心象牙制成。

sentences.en: And therefore, the average number of billiard balls that could be obtained from a single
sentences.zh: 因此，从一根象牙中平均可以获得的台球数量

sentences.en: tusk was three.
sentences.zh: 是三个。

sentences.en: If you are the best, luckiest billiard ball-turner, maybe you could get five balls from one tusk.
sentences.zh: 如果你是最好、最幸运的台球车工，也许你能从一根象牙里弄出五个球。

sentences.en: But even so, that means one set of billiard balls is going to require killing at least
sentences.zh: 即便如此，这也意味着制造一套台球需要杀死至少

sentences.en: two elephants.
sentences.zh: 两头大象。

sentences.en: So billiard balls were very expensive.
sentences.zh: 所以台球非常昂贵。

sentences.en: And when you're trying to build an industry, that's a problem.
sentences.zh: 当你想建立一个产业时，这就是个问题。

sentences.en: For Phelan's company, it was the problem.
sentences.zh: 对费兰的公司来说，这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: The entire trade depended on the sources of this one exotic material.
sentences.zh: 整个行业都依赖于这种单一珍奇材料的来源。

sentences.en: That's Robert Friedel, a professor at the University of Maryland.
sentences.zh: 那是马里兰大学的教授罗伯特·弗里德尔。

sentences.en: He studies the history of technology, and he wrote the book on what happens next.
sentences.zh: 他研究技术史，并且写了一本关于接下来发生的事情的书。

sentences.en: Phelan and his colleagues were acutely aware that their dependency on ivory was not ideal.
sentences.zh: 费兰和他的同事们敏锐地意识到，他们对象牙的依赖并不理想。

sentences.en: They're really desperate, I don't think it's too strong a word, to find some kind of
sentences.zh: 他们真的很绝望，我觉得用这个词并不过分，想要找到某种

sentences.en: substitute material, but that there simply wasn't anything.
sentences.zh: 替代材料，但根本找不到任何东西。

sentences.en: Phelan takes out an ad in the paper, and here's a dramatization of what happened when
sentences.zh: 费兰在报纸上登了一则广告，下面是对一个叫约翰·韦斯利·海亚特的人

sentences.en: a guy named John Wesley Hyatt found that ad.
sentences.zh: 看到那则广告时情景的戏剧化演绎。

sentences.en: Say, John, look at this.
sentences.zh: 听着，约翰，看这个。

sentences.en: Read it yourself.
sentences.zh: 你自己读读。

sentences.en: A prize of $10,000 for the discovery of a satisfactory substitute for ivory in making
sentences.zh: 悬赏1万元，寻找一种满意的象牙替代品来制造

sentences.en: billiard balls.
sentences.zh: 台球。

sentences.en: That's from a 1937 episode of a radio show called Cavalcade of America.
sentences.zh: 这是1937年一档名为《美国巡礼》的广播节目的片段。

sentences.en: Say, that's a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 哇，那可是一大笔钱。

sentences.en: It certainly is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: In terms of wages people earned at the time, it was like $3 million.
sentences.zh: 按当时人们的工资水平算，相当于300万美元。

sentences.en: Hyatt wasn't a chemist, but he was a tinkerer, and he worked for years to win Phelan's prize.
sentences.zh: 海亚特不是化学家，但他是个修补匠，他花了多年时间来赢得费兰的奖金。

sentences.en: By trade, Hyatt was a printer, and printers used nitrated cellulose to protect their hands.
sentences.zh: 海亚特的职业是印刷工，印刷工使用硝化纤维素来保护双手。

sentences.en: It's still sold as liquid bandages.
sentences.zh: 它现在仍然作为液体创可贴出售。

sentences.en: And that material turned out to have very interesting properties, and in particular,
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这种材料具有非常有趣的特性，特别是，

sentences.en: it dissolved, and it creates a very syrupy liquid.
sentences.zh: 它会溶解，并产生一种非常像糖浆的液体。

sentences.en: In the radio dramatization, Hyatt gets his key inspiration when a bottle of the stuff
sentences.zh: 在广播剧的戏剧化演绎中，海亚特的灵感来自于一瓶这种东西

sentences.en: overturns, and he watches it dry into a film that he finds interesting.
sentences.zh: 被打翻了，他看着它干燥成一层他觉得有趣的薄膜。

sentences.en: Why, this bit of film has given me an idea, and the idea it might be worth $10,000.
sentences.zh: 哎呀，这片薄膜给了我一个主意，这个主意可能值1万美元。

sentences.en: Hyatt's idea might have been worth $10,000, but it was also dangerous.
sentences.zh: 海亚特的主意可能值1万美元，但它也很危险。

sentences.en: Nitrated cellulose is highly, highly flammable.
sentences.zh: 硝化纤维素是高度高度易燃的。

sentences.en: You mean to say you're going to heat that nitrated cotton and compress it?
sentences.zh: 你是说你要加热那个硝化棉并对其进行压缩？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I'm going out of here.
sentences.zh: 我要离开这里。

sentences.en: Go as far away as I can before I start using that press.
sentences.zh: 在我开始使用那个压榨机之前，离得越远越好。

sentences.en: But John Hyatt and his lab assistant, Jim, kept going.
sentences.zh: 但约翰·海亚特和他的实验室助手吉姆继续坚持着。

sentences.en: They'd heat up the nitrated cotton, put it in the press, and...
sentences.zh: 他们加热硝化棉，把它放进压榨机里，然后……

sentences.en: Ready to open the press, John?
sentences.zh: 准备好打开压榨机了吗，约翰？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好了。

sentences.en: Throw the lever.
sentences.zh: 拉动杠杆。

sentences.en: John, what is it?
sentences.zh: 约翰，是什么？

sentences.en: Why don't you speak?
sentences.zh: 你怎么不说话？

sentences.en: What's the matter?
sentences.zh: 怎么回事？

sentences.en: Look, Jim.
sentences.zh: 看，吉姆。

sentences.en: It's making the press.
sentences.zh: 它成型了。

sentences.en: Look at it.
sentences.zh: 你看它。

sentences.en: Jim, it's what we've been trying to find all this time.
sentences.zh: 吉姆，这就是我们一直在寻找的东西。

sentences.en: A material that would take the place of ivory.
sentences.zh: 一种可以代替象牙的材料。

sentences.en: And the material that would take the place of ivory was plastic.
sentences.zh: 而能够取代象牙的材料就是塑料。

sentences.en: Hyatt called his new material celluloid.
sentences.zh: 海亚特把他的新材料命名为赛璐珞。

sentences.en: But celluloid did not win Phelan's $10,000 prize.
sentences.zh: 但赛璐珞并没有赢得费兰的1万美元奖金。

sentences.en: Celluloid is a wonderful material.
sentences.zh: 赛璐珞是一种奇妙的材料。

sentences.en: It's a beautiful plastic.
sentences.zh: 它是一种美丽的塑料。

sentences.en: It can be colored in all sorts of ways.
sentences.zh: 它可以被染成各种各样的颜色。

sentences.en: It can be shaped beautifully.
sentences.zh: 它可以被塑造成美丽的形状。

sentences.en: It has a wonderful range of uses.
sentences.zh: 它有着广泛的用途。

sentences.en: But billiard balls was not one of them.
sentences.zh: 但台球不在其中。

sentences.en: Balls made of celluloid just didn't bounce right.
sentences.zh: 用赛璐珞制作的球弹跳效果不对。

sentences.en: But Hyatt tried to make a go of it anyway.
sentences.zh: 但海亚特还是决定试一试。

sentences.en: He does set up a billiard ball company.
sentences.zh: 他确实开办了一家台球公司。

sentences.en: But his balls are not made of celluloid.
sentences.zh: 但他的球不是用赛璐珞做的。

sentences.en: They have a thin veneer of celluloid on the outside.
sentences.zh: 它们的外面有一层薄薄的赛璐珞贴面。

sentences.en: But they're mainly plaster on the inside.
sentences.zh: 但里面主要是石膏。

sentences.en: And they're very inferior by your ball.
sentences.zh: 而且它们的质量比你的球差远了。

sentences.en: Hyatt didn't give up on celluloid.
sentences.zh: 海亚特并没有放弃赛璐珞。

sentences.en: He went into business with his brother, Isaiah.
sentences.zh: 他和他的兄弟以赛亚一起合伙做生意。

sentences.en: The Hyatts set up a whole series of companies to try to exploit what they are convinced is a very nifty material.
sentences.zh: 海亚特兄弟成立了一系列公司，试图开发他们确信是一种非常棒的材料。

sentences.en: But they can't figure out what on earth the market's going to be.
sentences.zh: 但他们搞不清楚市场到底会是什么。

sentences.en: They try dental plates.
sentences.zh: 他们尝试了义齿托盘。

sentences.en: You can color celluloid to look just like real guMs.
sentences.zh: 你可以把赛璐珞染得看起来就像真正的牙龈一样。

sentences.en: But there's a problem.
sentences.zh: 但有个问题。

sentences.en: Turns out that celluloid gets soft if you're drinking hot tea.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，如果你喝热茶，赛璐珞会变软。

sentences.en: Eventually, they find the best use for celluloid is imitation ivory.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们发现赛璐珞最好的用途是仿制象牙。

sentences.en: Albeit not for billiard balls, but for versions of popular ivory luxury goods.
sentences.zh: 虽然不是用于台球，而是用于各种流行的象牙奢侈品。

sentences.en: Nice handles, combs, hand mirrors.
sentences.zh: 漂亮的把手、梳子、手镜。

sentences.en: Even toys and boxes, a gigantic range of things, many of which would never actually have been made in ivory.
sentences.zh: 甚至是玩具和盒子，种类繁多，其中许多原本根本不会用象牙制作。

sentences.en: Also, piano keys.
sentences.zh: 还有，钢琴键。

sentences.en: A Sears catalog from the 1890s offers pianos with a choice of key coverings, ivory or celluloid.
sentences.zh: 1890年代的西尔斯商品目录提供带有多种琴键外罩选择的钢琴，象牙或赛璐珞。

sentences.en: And of course, the most famous use of celluloid would eventually be to make film stock for movies.
sentences.zh: 当然，赛璐珞最著名的用途最终将是制造电影胶片。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, billiard balls kept getting made out of ivory.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，台球继续由象牙制成。

sentences.en: Ivory that came mostly from Africa, which of course the Europeans had been busy colonizing and exploiting.
sentences.zh: 这些象牙主要来自非洲，欧洲人当然一直在忙于殖民和剥削非洲。

sentences.en: And the ivory trade was pretty awful for the people of Africa.
sentences.zh: 象牙贸易对非洲人民来说相当残酷。

sentences.en: Joseph Conrad wrote Heart of Darkness, based largely on his own experience in the Belgian Congo, where ivory was the big product.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫·康拉德写了《黑暗的心》，很大程度上取材于他在比利时刚果的亲身经历，那里的主要产品就是象牙。

sentences.en: Conrad called the whole enterprise, quote,
sentences.zh: 康拉德把整场企业掠夺行为，原话形容为

sentences.en: The vilest scramble for loot that ever disfigured the history of human conscience.
sentences.zh: “人类良知史上最丑陋的战利品争夺战。”

sentences.en: And Conrad didn't necessarily care about this part, but obviously, the ivory trade was also terrible for elephants.
sentences.zh: 康拉德未必关心这一点，但显然，象牙贸易对大象来说也是一场灾难。

sentences.en: So what was, in fact, a pretty common animal in Central Africa in the middle of the 19th century is becoming increasingly scarce by the 20th.
sentences.zh: 因此，原本在19世纪中叶的中非地区相当常见的一种动物，到了20世纪变得越来越稀少。

sentences.en: By the time of World War I, the ivory supply crunch, the one that Michael Phelan had started worrying about 50 years before, had arrived.
sentences.zh: 到了第一次世界大战时，迈克尔·费兰在50年前就开始担忧的象牙供应危机终于降临了。

sentences.en: And around this time, the real significance of Hyatt's celluloid had begun to show itself.
sentences.zh: 也正是在这个时候，海亚特的赛璐珞的真正重要性开始显现出来。

sentences.en: It hadn't worked for billiard balls.
sentences.zh: 它不适用于台球。

sentences.en: However...
sentences.zh: 然而……

sentences.en: It began to inspire people to think about what artificial material might be available, what people could make, what people could invent.
sentences.zh: 它开始激发人们去思考可能会有什么样的人造材料可用，人们能制造什么，人们能发明什么。

sentences.en: In 1907, a chemist named Leo Bakeland comes up with a new kind of plastic made from petroleum.
sentences.zh: 1907年，一位名叫利奥·巴克兰的化学家发明了一种以石油为原料的新型塑料。

sentences.en: He names it Bakelite, after himself.
sentences.zh: 他用自己的名字将其命名为“电木”（Bakelite）。

sentences.en: And one cool thing about Bakelite, you can melt it, mix in fillers.
sentences.zh: 电木的一个酷炫之处在于，你可以把它融化，然后掺入填充物。

sentences.en: And it turns out that with that capability, you can vary the density, you can vary the elasticity, and you can make a perfect bigger ball.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，凭借这种性能，你可以改变它的密度，可以改变它的弹性，从而制造出完美的更大号球。

sentences.en: And so they finally replaced ivory balls with this new plastic, Bakelite.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们最终用这种名为电木的新塑料取代了象牙球。

sentences.en: By the 1940s, even top pool tournaments were being played with plastic balls.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪40年代，就连顶级的台球锦标赛也是用塑料球进行的。

sentences.en: But by then, pool had passed its peak.
sentences.zh: 但到那时，台球已经过了它的全盛时期。

sentences.en: It crashed as the Depression began, and never regained its former prominence.
sentences.zh: 随着大萧条的开始，它一落千丈，再也没有恢复往日的显赫地位。

sentences.en: The age of billiards was over.
sentences.zh: 台球时代结束了。

sentences.en: And this post-billiards age, the age of plastics, had really gotten into gear.
sentences.zh: 而这个后台球时代，即塑料时代，真正开始全面运转了。

sentences.en: For example, the handle of your toothbrush is probably plastic.
sentences.zh: 例如，你的牙刷柄很可能是塑料的。

sentences.en: So undoubtedly are the barrel of your fountain pen, the instrument panel in your car.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，你的钢笔杆、汽车上的仪表盘也是如此。

sentences.en: And yet these are just a few of more than 25,000 modern uses for plastics.
sentences.zh: 然而，这些只是塑料25000多种现代用途中的一小部分。

sentences.en: That's plastics, plural.
sentences.zh: 这就是塑料，复数形式。

sentences.en: By that time, you've got a bunch on the market.
sentences.zh: 到那时，市场上已经出现了一大批塑料。

sentences.en: PVC, vinyl, polyethylene, plexiglass, nylon.
sentences.zh: PVC、乙烯基、聚乙烯、有机玻璃、尼龙。

sentences.en: And in labs, they're discovering the stuff that would end up becoming Teflon and saran wrap.
sentences.zh: 在实验室里，他们正在发现最终将成为特氟龙和保鲜膜的材料。

sentences.en: In good old celluloid, the plastic that started it all had been retired, even from the movies.
sentences.zh: 曾经开创这一切的、老牌的赛璐珞塑料，甚至已经从电影界退役了。

sentences.en: It was indispensable to the beginning of motion pictures, but it was highly dangerous and flammable.
sentences.zh: 它对早期电影的发展至关重要，但它极度危险且易燃。

sentences.en: Celluloid film caused several disastrous and fatal fires in movie theaters.
sentences.zh: 赛璐珞胶片曾导致电影院发生几起灾难性的致命火灾。

sentences.en: By 1934, a new form, cellulose acetate, had taken the place of Hyatt's cellulose nitrate for film.
sentences.zh: 到了1934年，一种新形式的醋酸纤维素取代了海亚特的硝酸纤维素用于胶片。

sentences.en: Celluloid, born out of billiards, was the first plastic.
sentences.zh: 赛璐珞诞生于台球，是第一种塑料。

sentences.en: It ushered in a new age of modern products, but it never succeeded in revolutionizing the game of billiards.
sentences.zh: 它引领了一个现代产品的新时代，但它从未成功彻底革新台球运动。

sentences.en: It did, however, revolutionize another table sport.
sentences.zh: 不过，它确实革新了另一项桌上运动。

sentences.en: Ping pong.
sentences.zh: 乒乓球。

sentences.en: Before celluloid was invented, ping pong was played with something more closely resembling a golf ball, which, as you can imagine, just didn't have that perfect bounce.
sentences.zh: 在赛璐珞发明之前，乒乓球是用一种更类似于高尔夫球的东西来打的，正如你所想象的那样，它就是没有那种完美的弹跳。

sentences.en: Celluloid ping pong balls were used for years, but finally got bumped from tournament play in 2013.
sentences.zh: 赛璐珞乒乓球使用了多年，但最终在2013年被淘汰出锦标赛。

sentences.en: The reason?
sentences.zh: 原因呢？

sentences.en: They were a little too bouncy.
sentences.zh: 它们弹跳得有点太厉害了。

sentences.en: Poor celluloid.
sentences.zh: 可怜的赛璐珞。

sentences.en: It just can't win.
sentences.zh: 它就是无法胜出。

sentences.en: Someday we'll find the perfect home for you, my bouncy friend.
sentences.zh: 总有一天我们会为你找到一个完美的家，我那弹跳的朋友。

sentences.en: Watch the ball.
sentences.zh: 看着这个球。

sentences.en: Watch the way I climb around your hall.
sentences.zh: 看着我攀爬你大厅的方式。

sentences.en: Walking up walls.
sentences.zh: 漫步墙壁。

sentences.en: Sideways and I stall.
sentences.zh: 横向移动然后停滞。

sentences.en: Throw the web on you all.
sentences.zh: 把蜘蛛网抛向你们所有人。

sentences.en: Back up with a U-Haul.
sentences.zh: 开着U-Haul货车回来。

sentences.en: Wreck and rep like Eddie on an L.A.
sentences.zh: 像埃迪在洛杉矶街道上那样

sentences.en: strip with RuPaul.
sentences.zh: 与鲁保罗一起大肆破坏和巡游。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Dan Weissman, with Katie Mingle, Sam Greenspan, Avery Truffleman, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由丹·韦斯曼制作，合作者包括凯蒂·明格、萨姆·格林斯潘、艾弗里·特拉夫曼以及我，罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Dave Bond, who runs the Chicago Billiard Museum, an online museum which has an amazing collection of billiards-related documents, data, and images.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢运营芝加哥台球博物馆的戴夫·邦德，这是一个在线博物馆，拥有大量与台球相关的珍贵文档、数据和图片。

sentences.en: We'll have a link on our website.
sentences.zh: 我们将在官网上提供链接。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 KALW, San Francisco, and produced out of the offices of ArcSign, an architecture and interiors firm in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山91.7 KALW电台的一个项目，制作于加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心美丽的一家名为ArcSign的建筑与室内设计公司的办公室里。

sentences.en: You can find this show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到并点赞这个节目。

sentences.en: We're all on Twitter, Tumblr, Instagram, and Spotify.
sentences.zh: 我们都在Twitter、Tumblr、Instagram和Spotify上。

sentences.en: And you can see the Johnny Appleseed of Billiards, Michael Phelan's extremely unsettling neckbeard at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在99pi.org上看到台球界的约翰尼·阿普尔西德——迈克尔·费兰那令人极其不安的颈须。

sentences.en: I just want to say one word to you.
sentences.zh: 我只想对你说一个词。

sentences.en: Just one word.
sentences.zh: 就一个词。

sentences.en: Yes, sir.
sentences.zh: 好的，先生。

sentences.en: Are you listening?
sentences.zh: 你在听吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I am.
sentences.zh: 是的，我在听。

sentences.en: Plastics.
sentences.zh: 塑料。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: How do you mean?
sentences.zh: 这话怎么说？

sentences.en: There's a great future in plastics.
sentences.zh: 塑料有着广阔的前景。

sentences.en: Think about it.
sentences.zh: 好好想想吧。

sentences.en: Will you think about it?
sentences.zh: 你愿意考虑一下吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I will.
sentences.zh: 是的，我会的。

sentences.en: Enough said.
sentences.zh: 点到为止。

sentences.en: That's a deal.
sentences.zh: 就这么说定了。
